turns.en: Okay, this is a pretty special episode because we're celebrating 1 million subscribers on the AI Engineer YouTube channel. So go over there and subscribe if you haven't heard about it. Our guest is Mihail Eric, who is not only teaching the Modern Software Developer at Stanford, which is going viral right now for basically covering all the AI-native development practices, but he is also Head of AI at Monaco. So he's not only a teacher but a practitioner. And those of you coming to the AI Code Summit next week, it's going to be the celebration of all the extreme progress that you've seen in coding in the last year. I'm excited about all the themes of fighting slop, of system one models, and of increasing your ambition for major rewrites of basically everything that you've seen in code. There's never been a more exciting time to be an AI engineer. And with 1 million AI engineers, I think it's just getting started. So let's get into the interview.
turns.zh: 好，这期节目相当特别，因为我们在庆祝 AI Engineer YouTube 频道突破 100 万订阅。如果你还没听说过，就去那边订阅吧。我们的嘉宾是 Mihail Eric，他不仅在斯坦福讲授“现代软件开发者”这门课——这门课现在正在走红，基本上覆盖了所有 AI 原生开发实践——他还是 Monaco 的 AI 负责人。所以他不仅是老师，也是实践者。下周来参加 AI Code Summit 的朋友们，那将是对过去一年你在编程领域所见的所有极端进展的一次庆祝。我很期待这些主题：对抗 slop、系统一模型，以及提升你的雄心去对代码里你见过的一切做大规模重写。做 AI 工程师，从来没有比现在更激动人心的时刻。而有 100 万 AI 工程师，我觉得这才刚刚开始。那我们进入访谈吧。

turns.en: Okay, we're in the studio with Mihail Eric, adjunct professor at Stanford and Head of AI at Monaco. Welcome.
turns.zh: 好，我们在演播室，和斯坦福兼任教授、Monaco AI 负责人 Mihail Eric 在一起。欢迎。

turns.en: Thank you. I'm glad to be here.
turns.zh: 谢谢。很高兴来到这里。

turns.en: You caught our attention because of your course that you are refreshing for the third time—third time, second time?
turns.zh: 你引起我们注意，是因为你这门课正在第三次更新——第三次，还是第二次？

turns.en: CS146, the Modern Software Developer at Stanford.
turns.zh: CS146，斯坦福的“现代软件开发者”。

turns.en: This particular generation of junior developers, of junior engineers, of people that are now entering the workforce, will I think be the first kind of generation of that new shift. And I looked at the syllabus and I was like, this is everything we cover. So every now and then I like to invite people like yourself who cover a broad range of topics, and then we can sort of go topic by topic and give people the state of the art of each of these things, which I assume you're doing with all your guests anyway.
turns.zh: 这一代初级开发者、初级工程师、现在正进入职场的人，我觉得会是这次新转变的第一代。我看了课程大纲，心想：这就是我们覆盖的一切。所以我时不时喜欢邀请像你这样覆盖广泛主题的人，然后我们可以一个主题一个主题地聊，给大家讲讲每件事的最前沿，我猜你平时对所有嘉宾也是这么做的。

turns.en: For sure.
turns.zh: 当然。

turns.en: Tell us the history of the course. What made you want to spin out CS146?
turns.zh: 讲讲这门课的历史吧。是什么让你想开设 CS146？

turns.en: Yes, this is the second time it's being taught and I taught it for the first time last fall. So fall 2025. This was pre like Opus 4.5, 5.4, 6 days, but even before fall 2025 the course had been about a year in the making. The genesis of the class was November of 2024 and I had sort of had this idea that we're seeing all this stuff happening in coding agents and yes they were an earlier version of the coding agents but already it felt like there was something drastically changing in terms of how developers were doing their work, how quickly we were getting work done, all that fun stuff. And so at the time it was all just scattered blog posts, scattered things you could find online if you were trying to really get into the methodology of how to do these things. And so I had this idea like, hey, well, is there a way to kind of structure a curriculum around this? It's a little bit more formal.
turns.zh: 是的，这是第二次开课，我第一次教是去年秋天，2025 年秋。那是在 Opus 4.5、5.4、6 之前，但甚至在 2025 年秋之前，这门课已经酝酿了大约一年。这门课的起点是 2024 年 11 月，我当时有个想法：我们看到编码智能体领域发生了这么多事，是的，那还是编码智能体的早期版本，但已经感觉有些东西在剧烈变化——开发者做事的方式、我们完成工作的速度，诸如此类。当时这些东西都只是零散的博客文章、零散的网络资料，如果你想真正深入这些方法论的话。所以我就有了这个想法：嘿，有没有办法围绕这个构建一套课程？让它更正式一点。

turns.en: Had the idea and, you know, my own alma mater is Stanford and I always had this dream to go back and teach something and kind of pay it forward. I've always been very deep into education. I talked to Chip, who also taught a class—one of my good friends.
turns.zh: 有了这个想法，而且你知道，我的母校就是斯坦福，我一直梦想回去教点东西，把这份恩情传递下去。我一直对教育非常投入。我跟 Chip 聊过，她也教过一门课——是我的好朋友。

turns.en: Yeah. Chip. Exactly.
turns.zh: 对，Chip。没错。

turns.en: Spoke to her—she had taught, I guess, Designing Machine Learning Systems—and so asked her what that process was like and took a lot of inspiration from how she designed the curriculum and thought about getting something through the school. Put it together, spent about 9 to 10 months—this was now fall of 2024 through to mid to late 2025—got it through the committee, made a case for the class to exist. I had to put together a proposal and everything, and that took me to fall 2025 when I taught it for the first time, which was very well received. Students were really interested in it. There was even, I guess, a Business Insider article that was written about the class last year. And then yeah, this year a lot of things changed—I would say really coding agents, autonomous coding agents, really picked up in a way that we had not seen before. So it felt like it was time to do this again, refresh things, and then here we are.
turns.zh: 我跟她聊了——她教过《设计机器学习系统》——我问她那个流程是什么样的，从她设计课程的方式里获得了很多灵感，也思考了怎么让课程通过学校的审批。把它做出来，花了大约 9 到 10 个月——那是从 2024 年秋到 2025 年中后期——让它通过了委员会，为这门课的存在做了论证。我得准备一份提案之类的，然后到了 2025 年秋我第一次教这门课，反响非常好。学生们真的很感兴趣。去年甚至还有一篇 Business Insider 的文章写了这门课。然后今年，很多事情变了——我会说真正的编码智能体、自主编码智能体，以我们前所未见的方式发展起来了。所以感觉是时候再做一次、更新一下，然后就有了现在。

ts.sec: From last year's survey to this year's principles

turns.en: Meanwhile you're also Head of AI at Monaco, which is also a very buzzy startup.
turns.zh: 同时你还是 Monaco 的 AI 负责人，这也是一家非常热门的创业公司。

turns.en: Yes. Yes, we are. We're in the airwaves right now and having a fun time doing it.
turns.zh: 是的，是的。我们现在正处在风口浪尖，而且做得很开心。

turns.en: Yeah. So I do like that you're also, I guess, a practitioner. You guys are obviously implementing all this stuff at Monaco. Any principles or observations about just what you have changed from last year to this year at a high level?
turns.zh: 对。我挺喜欢你同时也是个实践者。你们显然在 Monaco 落地了所有这些。从高层面上讲，关于你从去年到今年改变了什么，有什么原则或观察吗？

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. I mean a ton. I think that when I reflect on what last year's version of the class was, coding agents had been around, but we were still in kind of that phase where companies were emerging that were tackling every single part of the SDLC. There was a coding agent for code review, there was a coding agent for spec design, there was a coding agent for SRE, and some of those companies still exist, of course, but it felt like last year it was a lot more about a broad tour of here's everywhere you can use coding agents. And in a way, a lot of the curriculum last year was geared toward exposure and this kind of survey, this kind of odyssey of sorts through, hey, everything that you knew about the SDLC is now changing because of AI.
turns.zh: 是的，是的，太多了。我想，当我回顾去年那版课程时，编码智能体已经存在了，但我们还处在那个阶段：公司纷纷涌现，去攻克 SDLC 的每一个环节。有做代码审查的编码智能体，有做规格设计的编码智能体，有做 SRE 的编码智能体，当然其中一些公司现在还在，但去年感觉更多是一次广泛的巡览——这里是你可以用编码智能体的所有地方。某种程度上，去年很多课程内容都偏向于曝光和这种概览，像是一场奥德赛之旅：嘿，你对 SDLC 所知的一切现在都因为 AI 而改变了。

turns.en: This year, I think there's some principles that are solidifying, right? The idea of very careful context engineering, the idea of really thinking through design and architecture as a way of handling really complex tasks. And so the nature of my class is it's not intended for the beginner programmer. It is not a replacement for traditional computer science in the sense of algorithms, and in fact a lot of those classes are prerequisites to what I'm doing here. But I do know that if you have a good foundation, going now toward applying that and using those principles in production environments, in the real world—that's something that I think is now at a place where, you know, at Monaco we deal with massive codebases. I help a lot of companies also with thinking through their massive codebase designs and things like that. And so really it's more of a practitioner's course for once the students have graduated or are now entering the workforce, how to be the most productive members of the workforce.
turns.zh: 今年，我觉得有些原则正在固化，对吧？比如非常细致的上下文工程，比如真正把设计和架构想透，作为处理非常复杂任务的方式。所以我的课的性质是：它不是给初学者的。它不是传统计算机科学在算法意义上的替代品，事实上很多这类课程是我这门课的先修课。但我确实知道，如果你有好的基础，现在朝着应用它、在真实世界的生产环境里运用这些原则的方向走——这件事我觉得已经到了一个阶段：你知道，在 Monaco 我们要处理庞大的代码库。我也帮很多公司梳理他们庞大代码库的设计之类的事情。所以它更像是一门实践者的课，面向学生毕业之后或刚进入职场时，如何成为职场中最高产的人。

turns.en: You said you're passionate about education. I feel like students in that phase of being in college are in a pretty interesting spot. Any advice and any take? Should people study computer science right now? Is Claude Code and Codex all we need? I want to hear your thoughts.
turns.zh: 你说你对教育很有热情。我觉得处在大学阶段的学生处在一个挺有意思的位置。有什么建议和看法吗？现在人们还应该学计算机科学吗？Claude Code 和 Codex 就是我们需要的全部了吗？我想听听你的想法。

turns.en: Yeah, there's a lot of anxiety from students, as you can probably imagine. What are you trying to communicate to them?
turns.zh: 是啊，你能想象到学生们有很多焦虑。你想向他们传达什么？

turns.en: I think a lot of what I'm trying to communicate this time around is that the anxiety is still here, and there was anxiety last year as well. But I want to make the case that a well-trained AI-native engineer—and I know that's a buzzy word, but let's dive into what aspects of that are most interesting—a well-trained AI-native engineer can be the most useful asset to any company around. This is the first week of class, and in the first lecture I say, hey, I really believe that every company needs you, but the floor is much higher. So you're entering as your first job out of school, but it's not sufficient to just be an L3 at Google, if you use that kind of leveling system. You have to generally be better than almost at the senior level. So how do we get there more quickly? I'm trying to say that there is still a core bit of foundational software engineering that is important—some of these core values of how software systems are built and the trade-offs of those systems. But beyond that, you as the humans should still be valuable, and the rest of the implementation details you can defer more often.
turns.zh: 这次我想传达的是，焦虑依然存在，去年也有焦虑。但我想论证的是，一个训练有素的 AI 原生工程师——我知道这是个流行词，但我们来深入探讨其中哪些方面最有趣——一个训练有素的 AI 原生工程师可以成为任何公司最有用的资产。这是开课第一周，在第一堂课上我说，我真的相信每家公司都需要你，但门槛高得多。所以你刚毕业进入职场，但如果用谷歌那种职级体系来类比，仅仅达到 L3 是不够的。你通常必须比高级别的人还要优秀。那么，我们如何更快地达到那个水平？我想说的是，仍然有一部分核心的基础软件工程很重要——关于软件系统如何构建以及这些系统的权衡的一些核心价值观。但除此之外，作为人类，你们仍然应该是有价值的，而其余的实现细节你可以更多地交给 AI。

turns.en: Yeah, this is something I've said before, which is almost like the controversial—it's the kind of thing you say to be spicy, but I almost genuinely believe it—which is most students are cooked. Some of them are going to be super valuable. I don't think it's a very popular thing. Stanford kids are going to be fine, right? They're from Stanford. But like what happens to the rest of America?
turns.zh: 是的，这是我之前说过的话，几乎像是争议性的——那种为了制造话题而说的话，但我几乎真的相信——那就是大多数学生完蛋了。他们中的一些人会非常有价值。我不认为这是一个很受欢迎的观点。斯坦福的孩子会没事的，对吧？他们来自斯坦福。但美国其他地方的人会怎样？

turns.en: Right, that is an open question.
turns.zh: 是啊，这是一个开放的问题。

turns.en: Weird situation, because I feel like a lot of education is slow to move. I'm even curious how you determine where to put the end date to curriculum in a course—you're teaching a Stanford modern software course that's changing everything.
turns.zh: 奇怪的情况，因为我觉得很多教育机构行动缓慢。我甚至好奇你如何确定课程内容的截止日期——你在斯坦福教一门现代软件课程，而一切都在变化。

turns.en: You cheat—you just get the people from the coding agents to come and speak.
turns.zh: 你作弊——你直接请编码智能体公司的人来演讲。

turns.en: Oh yeah, have them be the guest. That's a funny guest.
turns.zh: 哦对，让他们当嘉宾。那是个有趣的嘉宾。

turns.en: It's funny. Well, on the guest lectures point, that was also last year, so that was by design. I came in saying I'm a practitioner, as you point out—I do this thing day-to-day, I design these systems, we build these things at Monaco and have seen that many times before. That being said, I don't want to claim that I have all the answers today—that would be a lot of hubris. So the structure of the class was always: here's one practitioner's aggregated set of insights from working in the field, from talking to a lot of people in the field, but then there are people who are literally on the frontier, seeing things even beyond that, and invite them to put their proposals forward, their view of the world forward. That's why the guest lectures.
turns.zh: 有趣。关于嘉宾讲座这一点，去年也是这样，所以这是有意设计的。我一开始就说我是从业者，正如你指出的——我每天都在做这件事，我设计这些系统，我们在 Monaco 构建这些东西，以前见过很多次。话虽如此，我不想声称我今天拥有所有答案——那会非常傲慢。所以课程的结构一直是：这里有一个从业者从实地工作中、从与许多领域内人士交谈中汇总的见解，但还有那些真正处于前沿的人，看到更远的东西，邀请他们提出他们的方案、他们对世界的看法。这就是为什么有嘉宾讲座。

turns.en: I think it's really impactful for students to see big names, people actually doing it, hear from them directly, be able to ask them—of course they want to intern, they want to get jobs. It's good to have guest lectures.
turns.zh: 我认为对学生来说，看到大牌人物、真正在做这件事的人，直接听他们讲，能够问他们问题，是非常有影响力的——当然他们想实习、想找工作。有嘉宾讲座是好事。

turns.en: No, I think what he's saying—okay, I'll rephrase. We've also interviewed someone who teaches the Coachella course, right? Which is like here's all the names—it's only the names—whereas he's actually also producing, here's Claude Code in 200 lines of code. No one's telling you to do that; no one's going to come speak to you about that. But when you want to teach fundamentals in a framework that you can use and a working understanding, this is the kind of thing you do.
turns.zh: 不，我想他说的——好吧，我换个说法。我们也采访过教 Coachella 课程的人，对吧？那就像是这里全是名字——只有名字——而他实际上也在产出，比如用 200 行代码实现 Claude Code。没人告诉你要那样做；没人会来跟你讲那个。但当你想在一个你可以使用的框架中教授基础知识，并建立工作理解时，这就是你要做的事情。

turns.en: That's right. That's right. Yeah. Yeah. Exactly.
turns.zh: 没错。没错。是的。是的。正是如此。

turns.en: And I do think there's a balance for this kind of material, to your point—it's not 100% solidified. By design, it's a feature and maybe a bug of some kind, but a big portion of the curriculum did change from last year. So there's a dynamism to the whole development of the curriculum. But I'm trying to at least put forth that there are some things that I believe are sticking around, and yes, prompting coding agents—they've gotten smarter. What does that mean in terms of new ways of dealing with them? But then still Boris is also going to know something that I don't know, right? So let's have him also come to the table and share his learnings.
turns.zh: 我确实认为这类材料需要平衡，正如你所说——它不是 100% 固化的。从设计上讲，这是一个特性，也许某种程度也是个缺陷，但课程的大部分内容确实从去年发生了变化。所以整个课程开发具有动态性。但我至少试图提出一些我认为会持续存在的东西，是的，提示编码智能体——它们变得更聪明了。这在处理它们的新方式方面意味着什么？但 Boris 也会知道一些我不知道的东西，对吧？所以让他也来分享他的学习成果。

ts.sec: Open Source Contributions in the Course

turns.en: One of the fun things I noticed this time around is a good bit of the portion is on open source contributions. What's the thinking behind that?
turns.zh: 这次我注意到的一个有趣的事情是，很大一部分内容是关于开源贡献的。这背后的思考是什么？

turns.en: Yeah, this is one of the things that I'm honestly most proud of and most excited about. This is about to be week two of the class. So this is the very gracious open source partners that I spent the greater part of this summer just talking to and getting them excited about and interested in this offering. Basically, the idea was: last year when I taught the class we had nine assignments and then a capstone open-ended project. The nine assignments were basically me coming up with these pedagogical exercises—like, here's a repo, use an AI code review tool to post a code review and then see why is it good, why is it not good. Relatively pedagogical, honestly pretty easy. I think for a lot of folks they could have just one-shot it. And I thought, okay, this is not that helpful at this point—agents are around. Every student that I surveyed on Tuesday—not a single person really types by hand anymore; everyone's using coding agents. And this is, you know, all sophomores, juniors at Stanford.
turns.zh: 是的，这是我老实说最自豪、最兴奋的事情之一。这将是课程的第二周。这些是非常慷慨的开源合作伙伴，我花了这个夏天的大部分时间与他们交谈，让他们对这个项目感到兴奋和感兴趣。基本上，想法是：去年我教这门课时，我们有九个作业，然后是一个开放式的顶点项目。那九个作业基本上是我设计的一些教学练习——比如，这里有一个代码库，使用 AI 代码审查工具发布代码审查，然后看看为什么好，为什么不好。相对教学化，老实说相当简单。我认为很多人可以一次性完成。我想，好吧，在智能体已经存在的现在，这没那么有帮助。我周二调查的每个学生——没有一个人真正手动打字了；每个人都在使用编码智能体。这些都是斯坦福的大二、大三学生。

turns.en: Do you survey them? What's the market share?
turns.zh: 你调查他们吗？市场份额是多少？

turns.en: Was that like what tools they use? Okay. I haven't yet, but that's a good call. Yeah. I will.
turns.zh: 你是说他们使用什么工具吗？好的。我还没有，但这是个好主意。是的。我会的。

turns.en: Be spicy. Stanford prefers.
turns.zh: 来点劲爆的。斯坦福偏爱。

turns.en: No. No.
turns.zh: 不。不。

turns.en: Well, I think through the university, they have some educational program, right? Most of the providers have an educational program.
turns.zh: 嗯，我觉得通过大学，他们有一些教育项目，对吧？大多数提供商都有教育项目。

turns.en: Yeah, they're very generous on plans for students, right?
turns.zh: 是的，他们对学生计划非常慷慨，对吧？

turns.en: Right. So I think by default even before the class there's like a Claude license, I imagine a Cursor license, there's probably a Cognition license as well. I don't know, you might know that better than I do. But what I was able to also accrue on top of that was, hey, if I don't want people to be bottlenecked by the $20 a month subscription, I want you guys to go if you want to token max something just to see what's possible, then you should. And so, and I'll come back to the partners, but the additional thing I was able to accrue through instead of talking to folks was additional credits for students. So Factory is also getting involved. The Cognition folks are getting involved and OpenAI as well.
turns.zh: 对。所以我认为默认情况下，甚至在课程开始之前，就有 Claude 许可证，我猜还有 Cursor 许可证，可能还有 Cognition 许可证。我不太确定，你可能比我更了解。但除此之外，我还争取到了：嘿，如果我不想让人们因为每月 20 美元的订阅而受限，我希望你们如果想把 token 用到极致，看看能做什么，那就去做。所以，我稍后会回到合作伙伴的话题，但我通过与人交谈争取到的额外东西是给学生的额外额度。所以 Factory 也参与进来了。Cognition 的人参与进来了，OpenAI 也是。

turns.en: But anyway, so for the open source partners, I was like, okay, one of the things I'm most concerned about when it comes to educating the next generation of students is that if everyone is saying, to Six's point, like they're cooked, you know what's going to happen to them there. There's almost this sense of them being left behind. And I think that mentorship is a really important piece of just upleveling everyone and making sure that there isn't this massive gap that occurs between the senior people that have already been in the industry before coding agents and know what's up, and they adopt coding agents and they become amazing, and then the juniors that are just like, okay, now what do we do? So in a sense, one of the goals was, hey, coding agents are really good. I want to put you guys in situations where you're dealing with complex code bases, large code bases at scale. We're going to work with some of what I think are among the best AI native repos, you know, that all do AI focused things or either coding agents themselves or building tools in the service of agents in the modern world. I want you guys to get involved with these projects. I want part of your assignments to be actually contributing to these projects. In the course of being involved with those projects, you will actually be talking to the maintainers. They will be reviewing your code. They will be helping you build mental models of good software. In that way, there's effectively this passing on of the guard of true good software design in a way that I don't think most students get the opportunity to do. And then there's the benefit, of course, that I'm sure some of them will get poached and picked up as part of doing well in those assignments.
turns.zh: 但不管怎样，所以对于开源合作伙伴，我想，好吧，我在教育下一代学生时最担心的一件事是，如果每个人都说，就像 Six 说的，他们完蛋了，你知道他们会怎样。几乎有一种他们被落下的感觉。我认为导师制是提升每个人水平、确保不会出现巨大差距的重要一环，这个差距出现在那些已经在行业里、在编码智能体之前就了解情况并采用编码智能体变得很厉害的资深人士，和那些刚说“好吧，现在我们该怎么办？”的初级人士之间。所以某种意义上，一个目标是：嘿，编码智能体真的很棒。我想把你们置于处理复杂代码库、大规模大型代码库的情境中。我们将与一些我认为是最好的 AI 原生仓库合作，你知道，它们都做 AI 相关的事情，要么是编码智能体本身，要么是为智能体构建工具。我希望你们参与这些项目。我希望你们的作业一部分是实际为这些项目做贡献。在参与这些项目的过程中，你们将实际与维护者交谈。他们会审查你的代码。他们会帮助你建立良好软件的心智模型。这样，实际上就传递了真正优秀软件设计的火炬，我认为大多数学生没有机会这样做。当然还有好处，我确信有些人会因为在这些作业中表现出色而被挖走。

turns.en: Yeah. One of the interesting things, for what it's worth, I'll get a bunch of hate if I don't say this. I think you say 'cooked' versus 'cracked' for dramatic effect, but you know, it's just nice to state extremes.

turns.en: Sure. Sure.

turns.en: Sure. Sure. Yeah. So we start with internals and coding agents. You teach people how to write their own Claude Code clone. It's very helpful that it's now open source. And then, yeah, yeah, yeah, so week one it's all internals of harnesses, you know, kind of build a coding agent from scratch. Week two is more, okay, now assume that there's, how do we start thinking about context engineering at scale, beyond just vanilla prompting. And then I think coupled with that is just in doing that, thinking about tool design, MCP. You know, people, I think for a while MCP was getting a lot of hate. I'm still pro MCP. I see it all the time. And so I think that there's, at this point it's a standard that's existed and I think it will continue to exist. So talking about that effective tool design, that's week two. Week three I would say is more about just like skills and what does it mean to extend beyond simple single purpose tools to more like procedures, and that's where we'll talk about skills and that kind of starts leading into the automation of agents.
turns.zh: 当然。当然。是的。所以我们从内部机制和编码智能体开始。你教人们如何编写自己的 Claude Code 克隆。它现在是开源的，这非常有帮助。然后，是的，是的，是的，所以第一周全是 harness 的内部机制，你知道，从头构建一个编码智能体。第二周更多是，好吧，现在假设有，我们如何开始思考大规模的上下文工程，超越普通的提示。然后我认为与此相结合的是，在做这件事时，思考工具设计、MCP。你知道，人们，我认为有一段时间 MCP 受到很多批评。我仍然支持 MCP。我经常看到它。所以我认为，在这一点上它是一个已经存在的标准，我认为它将继续存在。所以谈论有效的工具设计，那是第二周。第三周我会说更多是关于技能，以及超越简单的单一用途工具到更多程序化意味着什么，这就是我们将讨论技能的地方，这开始引导到智能体的自动化。

turns.en: Week four is a lot of just more of the foundational pieces of how can you customize an agent? This is things like agent config files, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, hooks, subagents. There are a lot of different mechanisms that exist in modern harnesses which you can use for different purposes. So I want to expose students to that.
turns.zh: 第四周主要是更多关于如何定制智能体的基础内容。这包括智能体配置文件、AGENTS.md、CLAUDE.md、钩子、子智能体等。现代框架中有很多不同的机制，你可以用于不同目的。所以我想让学生接触这些。

turns.en: Agent-ready codebases. This is probably one of my favorite topics. This is especially relevant for folks that are going into industry and thinking about code at scale. Essentially, what does it mean to have a repo that's ready to be ingested and consumed effectively by an agent? So thinking a lot about the trade-offs of designing service-level boundaries, but also docs and verifiability and things of that nature. So that's week five.
turns.zh: 智能体就绪的代码库。这可能是我最喜欢的话题之一。这对那些进入工业界并思考大规模代码的人尤其相关。本质上，什么才算是一个准备好被智能体有效摄取和使用的代码库？所以要大量思考设计服务级边界的权衡，还有文档、可验证性之类的东西。这就是第五周。

turns.en: Week six is sort of agentic code review. And here I think what is interesting is thinking also kind of extending from week five—week five around agent-ready codebases—going to week six is more about: okay, in order to—code review is now becoming a bottleneck. I don't know that students—unless they have done a lot—some of them are master's students so they've been in the industry, but a lot of them have not seen this. But for most people that are using code agents today, we're all experiencing something of a new bottleneck in code review. So how do we unblock that or sort of unbottleneck the bottleneck a little bit? What mechanisms are there there? And so verifiability and things of that nature, and how we can extend that into the code review process.
turns.zh: 第六周是智能体式代码审查。这里我觉得有趣的是，从第五周延伸——第五周围绕智能体就绪的代码库——到第六周更多是：好的，为了——代码审查现在正成为瓶颈。我不知道学生们——除非他们做过很多——有些是硕士生，所以他们在工业界待过，但很多人没见过这个。但对于今天大多数使用代码智能体的人来说，我们都在经历代码审查的新瓶颈。那么我们如何解除这个瓶颈，或者稍微缓解瓶颈？有哪些机制？还有可验证性之类的东西，以及我们如何将其扩展到代码审查流程中。

turns.en: Week seven: security. I mean, obviously I think there was a point—so this was in last year's class as well and I wanted to reinforce this. I mean, with any autonomous system taking a lot of actions, we're seeing a lot of this year—especially a lot of things getting hacked, not least of which are just some of the core pieces of software from Vercel to LM gateways entirely. So I want to spend some time just talking about what new attack vectors exist in security and how we can mitigate some of them.
turns.zh: 第七周：安全。我的意思是，显然我认为有一个点——所以这也在去年的课上出现过，我想强调这一点。我的意思是，对于任何采取大量行动的自主系统，我们今年看到很多——尤其是很多东西被黑，不仅仅是 Vercel 的一些核心软件，还有 LM 网关完全被黑。所以我想花些时间谈谈安全中存在哪些新的攻击向量，以及我们如何缓解其中一些。

turns.en: Week eight is background agents. So this is what I want to start touching on here is: how do you basically run agents in many different product service areas? Not just in what was traditionally an IDE, but also having things that are based on triggers in your codebase, in your repo, during CI/CD, things that get triggered even based on events, things like SRE-style bots. How do you even build a system like—I think this past year was when a lot of companies started releasing their posts like Ramp, Inspect—there was Spotify has their own version of this, I think Stripe Minions—so all these folks were doing really cool write-ups of their internal info they were building to do this. I wanted to touch on that, get people exposed to what that is.
turns.zh: 第八周是后台智能体。所以这是我想开始涉及的：你基本上如何在许多不同的产品服务领域运行智能体？不仅仅是在传统的 IDE 中，还有基于代码库、仓库中的触发器，在 CI/CD 期间，甚至基于事件触发的东西，比如 SRE 风格的机器人。你甚至如何构建这样一个系统——我想过去一年是很多公司开始发布他们的文章的时候，比如 Ramp、Inspect——Spotify 有他们自己的版本，我想还有 Stripe Minions——所以所有这些人都写了非常酷的关于他们内部构建的信息。我想谈谈这个，让人们了解那是什么。

turns.en: Yeah, this one is more on what happens when you're in a team in the modern world and sort of the core pieces of team-level infrastructure. So everything from LM gateways to MCP portals, which is like MCP at scale, and then also how to think about the evolving roles, I would say. So this is maybe a little bit like a soft thing. It's like what is now—and the vanilla, maybe not super nuanced thing to say is like everyone's a builder, but I want to go a little bit deeper beyond that and sort of like what thing is actually getting subsumed, what roles are actually either evolving or emerging that didn't once exist. What should students think about in terms of defensible skill set that's maybe wasn't true before? And so a lot more like team dynamic type considerations.
turns.zh: 是的，这一周更多是关于在现代世界中你在团队中会发生什么，以及团队级基础设施的核心部分。所以从 LM 网关到 MCP 门户，也就是大规模 MCP，然后还有如何思考不断演变的角色，我想说。所以这也许有点像软性的东西。就像现在是什么——而 vanilla 的、也许不是超级细致的说法是每个人都是构建者，但我想更深入一点，超越这一点，比如什么东西实际上被吸收了，哪些角色实际上要么在演变，要么在出现以前不存在的东西。学生应该思考什么是可辩护的技能组合，也许以前不是这样？所以更多是团队动态类型的考虑。

ts.sec: The Software Factory and Human Involvement

turns.en: And then yeah, this all kind of builds up toward the factory, which I think is top of mind for a lot of folks today. Once we're building factories, where do humans still exist in all that? What is—where are the new choke points that are intentionally there around human involvement, things like intent, things like setting up verifiable systems, and what happens in the limit when maybe 80-90% of code is fully driven by just agents? Where we kind of filled into all that. So yeah, nice solid 10 weeks.
turns.zh: 然后是的，这一切都朝着工厂发展，我认为这是今天很多人最关心的事情。一旦我们建造工厂，人类在其中还存在于哪里？什么是——新的瓶颈点在哪里，这些瓶颈点有意围绕人类参与，比如意图，比如建立可验证系统，以及在极限情况下会发生什么，当也许 80-90% 的代码完全由智能体驱动时？我们有点填补了所有这些。所以是的，不错的扎实的 10 周。

turns.zh: 当然。但这一切——我会认可所有这些都是人们谈论的事情，你应该知道。我们只是——我们知道开放问题，我们可能不知道答案。

turns.en: Like just spending some 10 minutes doing something that you didn't do before. turns.zh: 比如花 10 分钟做一件你以前没做过的事。如果那是你过去解决问题的方式，现在有了新工具或新框架，哪怕只是用新东西做完全相同的问题，单是这一点就能弥补大部分差距。

ts.sec: The software factory and the human in the loop

turns.en: So there are a few aspects here. Okay, so there's a little bit of spillover from the previous week — coding agents, big teams, some of the concepts — but then we'll touch on the software factory. I want people to really start thinking about this world of this machine that builds the machine, and where, if at all, people are still in the loop there. You know, today I think the answer is some combination of intent and kind of review — maybe the places like intent, where you're defining the specs and what needs to be built, and review, where you're doing some amount of your own checking of the system. And of course this — I think that bottleneck is going to be loosened up before even the intent piece does. But for now those are the two choke points, I think, in a fully automated system. So yeah, I just want to give people exposure — one of the OSS partners, actually Warp, they're doing this thing as part of their contribution to the OSS program, where they're going to essentially make a version of Warp that is running the factory, and students will just be like building the factory, contributing to the factory, and keeping it running.
turns.zh: 这里有几个方面。好，所以有一点上周内容的延续——编码智能体、大团队、一些概念——但接下来我们会谈到软件工厂。我想让大家真正开始思考这个“制造机器的机器”的世界，以及人在其中到底还在不在环里。你知道，今天我认为答案是意图和某种审查的组合——也许是意图，你在这里定义规格和要建什么；以及审查，你在这里自己对系统做一些检查。当然，这个——我觉得这个瓶颈会比意图那部分更早被松开。但就目前而言，我认为在一个完全自动化的系统里，这是两个卡点。所以对，我就是想让大家接触一下——其中一个开源合作伙伴，其实是 Warp，他们在为开源项目做贡献时做这件事：他们基本上会做一个运行工厂的 Warp 版本，学生们就负责建工厂、给工厂做贡献、让它持续运行。

consensus.en: AI-native engineers need strong software foundations; the floor is higher, but they can be a company's most valuable asset.
consensus.zh: AI 原生工程师需要扎实的软件基础；门槛更高，但他们可以成为公司最有价值的资产。

consensus.en: Context engineering with research, proposal, and spec phases is essential for large codebases.
consensus.zh: 对于大型代码库，包含研究、提案和规格阶段的上下文工程至关重要。

consensus.en: Agent-ready codebases—verifiable, well-structured, understandable—are the foundation for multi-agent and software factories.
consensus.zh: 智能体就绪的代码库——可验证、结构良好、易于理解——是多智能体和软件工厂的基础。

consensus.en: Code review is the new bottleneck; we need a middle ground between full human review and auto-approval.
consensus.zh: 代码审查是新的瓶颈；我们需要在完全人工审查和自动批准之间找到中间地带。

consensus.en: Security must focus on dependency tracking and supply chain; not all code deserves equal scrutiny—data and billing are critical.
consensus.zh: 安全必须关注依赖跟踪和供应链；并非所有代码都值得同等审查——数据和计费是关键。

consensus.en: Build to learn and buy to keep: build in-house when no mature offering exists, otherwise leverage vendors.
consensus.zh: 构建以学习，购买以保持：没有成熟产品时自建，否则利用供应商。

contrarian.en: Most students are cooked, but a well-trained AI-native engineer can be a company's most valuable asset.
contrarian.zh: 大多数学生完蛋了，但训练有素的 AI 原生工程师可以成为公司最有价值的资产。

contrarian.en: Skills feel sloppy; some at Anthropic may want them to die, though not publicly.
contrarian.zh: 技能感觉草率；Anthropic 的一些人可能希望它们消亡，尽管不会公开说。

contrarian.en: The safest codebase may have no dependencies; building everything in-house could be more secure.
contrarian.zh: 最安全的代码库可能没有依赖；自建一切可能更安全。

contrarian.en: MCP portals will fold into LM gateways; they are the same platform layer.
contrarian.zh: MCP 门户将并入 LM 网关；它们是同一平台层。

contrarian.en: Models introduce different bugs, not necessarily fewer; the real risk is reduced awareness of what's written.
contrarian.zh: 模型引入不同的错误，不一定更少；真正的风险是对所写内容缺乏了解。

contrarian.en: Most companies will evolve into coding agent companies, closing the loop from user insight to product fix.
contrarian.zh: 大多数公司将演变为编码智能体公司，从用户洞察到产品修复形成闭环。
